blocks.text: Lesson 5 — Vulnerability assessment and risk prioritization

LEARNING OUTCOME
Validate scanner output, identify false positives, estimate impact and recommend fixes.

Safety rule: work only with devices, accounts and training applications you own or have explicit written permission to assess. Use synthetic information. A public system or a suspicious person is not permission.

Tools may flag outdated versions or settings, but findings can be false positives or duplicate symptoms. Validate asset identity, version source, configuration and patch status safely. Do not use intrusive proof-of-concept code just to make a scanner result look important.

blocks.text: Consider exposure, privileges required, business criticality, data sensitivity, compensating controls and evidence that a vulnerability is exploited. CVSS helps describe technical severity but does not fully represent business risk. Use the owner’s model and current advisories to set remediation order.

blocks.caption: Visual 3/6 — False positives. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.
Visual 4/6 — Impact estimate. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.

blocks.text: Include safe reproduction steps, expected and observed behavior, impact, affected configuration, mitigation and retest criteria. Redact personal data and secrets; reports belong only in approved channels.

blocks.caption: Visual 5/6 — Priority order. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.
Visual 6/6 — Remediation. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.

blocks.text: Practice checklist: (1) read the lab rules, (2) use fabricated data or an isolated training target, (3) predict what the control should do, (4) test one small condition, (5) save only minimal evidence, and (6) explain the defensive follow-up. Stop and ask the owner if any target or action is outside the approved scope.

blocks.output: Validate safely before prioritizing a possible issue.

blocks.question: Before Lesson 5 testing, what should be confirmed?
options: A friend said it is okay
The exact target is covered by written permission
blocks.explanation: Written permission should define target and allowed methods.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: How should a finding from Lesson 5 be handled?
options: Include a real password as proof
Save minimal redacted evidence and report through the approved channel
blocks.explanation: Findings need scoped, protected and reproducible evidence.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: What requires the learner to stop?
options: Target is out of scope or testing may cause unexpected harm
A lab result needs an explanation
blocks.explanation: Stop if scope or safety limits may be crossed.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: What is a sound step after applying a fix?
options: Retest the same authorized condition and document the result
blocks.explanation: Retesting verifies the correction and preserves a useful record.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: What should happen when a target is outside scope?
options: Stop and ask the owner to clarify permission
blocks.explanation: Scope is a boundary; do not proceed without permission.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.
